reason: The original decision treated biomimetic hardware coding as substantive AI too broadly. The abstract describes light encoding, neurotransmitter modulation and a retinal pathway primitive; it does not establish learning, inference, recognition or an AI-supported scientific task. Remove the spiking neural network tag.

Mechanical gating, leaky integrate-and-fire models and transistor circuits mimic tactile nerves and perform acquisition and rendering. A closed acquisition/rendering loop is not itself learned feedback. No AI recognition or inference is established; the same pure biomimetic-device boundary as index 43 applies.
The abstract explicitly trains a multivariate predictive fMRI brain model and tests it across nine samples. Add the existing generic Machine learning label without inferring a specific architecture.

Conservative, medium-confidence suggestion: spectral inversion is a clear engineering task, but AI evidence consists only of the Neural Spectral Fields name and use of a responsivity matrix. The abstract does not describe learning or trainable representations. This may indeed be a neural implicit method, so do not exclude outright; the lead reviewer should decide whether the named method is sufficient abstract evidence.
